Reviewed the finding — all 5 items are Artificial Analysis / Hugging Face entries for models that don't have a matching row (Claude Fable 5.1, Muse Spark 1.3 ×2 variants, Gemini 3.8 Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp). I confirmed by grep that none of these already exist under a different name (only "Fable 5" and "Muse Spark 1.2" exist, not 5.1/1.3), so these are genuine additions, not renames or drift.

**Summary of this run:**

- **Scores that moved or arrived:** none. The board-reconciliation section only flagged unmatched model names (all out of scope, see below) — no existing row had a stale or blank AA score to update.
- **Dead or moved links:** none confirmed dead. 2 targets were unreachable during the check (network-level, not identified by name), so nothing to repoint — the check itself distinguishes "unreachable" from "dead," and I have no target to act on.
- **Config drift:** none. Every `SPECS` entry still matches its `config.json`; 1 target was unreachable and not checked (again, no identified target to follow up on).
- **Left for a human, and why:** all 5 findings are new-model additions — Claude Fable 5.1, Muse Spark 1.3 (max and xhigh), Gemini 3.8 Flash (high), and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp on Hugging Face. None have existing rows in the atlas. Adding a row requires judgment (architecture provenance, whether a preview's figures will hold, whether it's in scope as a language model) that this mechanical job isn't set up to exercise, per `CLAUDE.md`.

No file changes were made. `node scripts/verify/maps.mjs` was run for confirmation and passes clean (0 structural problems, 83 models). Since nothing changed, there's nothing to commit or push, and no live-site check is needed.
